Changelog

New updates and improvements to DeepCleanMac.

October 19, 2026

Version 1.7.3
Fix
cleaning Power Logs no longer deletes any of macOS's live power databases; only old archived records are cleaned
New
old macOS and xrOS debug files in Xcode Device Support are now cleaned, keeping the two newest of each

October 15, 2026

Version 1.7.2
Fix
update copies waiting to install no longer show up as a second copy of the app in the Uninstaller
Improved
Uninstalls now also remove the app's crash-reporter folder and its folder in the macOS system cache
Improved
Uninstalling Claude Desktop now removes its "Claude-3p" folders
Improved
Symantec, Broadcom and Alibaba Cloud Security software can only be removed with the vendor's own uninstaller

October 13, 2026

Version 1.7.1
Fix
Offline Spotify music is safe — Spotify keeps the songs you download for offline listening inside its cache folder, so cleaning that cache could delete your downloads. The Spotify cache is no longer cleaned.
Fix
Prometheus metrics are no longer lost — the Prometheus write-ahead log was treated as a cache, but it holds recent metrics that haven't been saved anywhere else yet. It's now always left alone.
Fix
Your current iOS debug files stay — Xcode Device Support always keeps the two newest versions, but it counted them across every device type together. A newer watchOS or tvOS version could push out the iOS version you're still using. The two newest are now kept for each device type separately.
Improved
Safer cleanup for developers — build folders in your projects were sometimes not recognised as holding files committed to Git, for example after a folder was renamed only by changing its capital letters. Those folders are now kept like any other folder with committed files.
Improved
No surprise iCloud downloads — when your projects folder is in iCloud Drive, the project scan now skips folders that are stored only in the cloud. Before, just scanning them made macOS download them.
Improved
Safer uninstalls for Epic Games apps — uninstalling one app could also match the shared Epic folder in Application Support, which holds engines, assets and licence data used by other Epic apps. That folder is now always left alone.
New
More developer files covered — the Cleaner now finds old visionOS debug files in Xcode Device Support, and cached Apple TV software updates next to the iPhone and iPad ones.

October 7, 2026

Version 1.7.0
Fix
Crash reports are saved again after a clean — cleaning your logs could remove the folder macOS saves crash reports in. macOS can't recreate that folder on its own, so new crash reports were quietly lost from then on. The old reports are still cleaned, but the folder now stays.
Fix
Live Text keeps working after a clean — macOS keeps a small cache that powers text recognition in images, Live Text and parts of Spotlight. Clearing it while those were running could break them until the app was restarted. It's now always left alone, and it frees almost no space anyway.
Improved
Safer cleanup for developers — build folders in your coding projects are now checked before they're offered for cleaning. A folder is kept if it holds its own Git repository, a deploy key, or files you've committed to Git. It's also kept whenever DeepCleanMac can't finish checking it.
New
Crash reports have their own category — they now appear as "User Crash Reports" in the Cleaner, separate from User Logs, so you can see what they take up and clean them on their own.

October 1, 2026

Version 1.6.9
Fix
Minor bug fixes

September 30, 2026

Version 1.6.8
Fix
Safer cleaning for R users — the R cache folder is no longer cleared. renv keeps its installed packages there and links every project to them, so emptying it left R projects unable to load their packages. The folder is now always left alone.

September 28, 2026

Version 1.6.7
Fix
More accurate scan sizes — some cache folders were counted twice, so a scan could report far more space than it would actually free. Chrome's cache is also no longer cleared while Chrome is open, and Poetry's virtual environments are left alone.

September 22, 2026

Version 1.6.6
Improved
Safer cleaning around open apps — whether an app is running is now checked the moment you pick it, not only when the scan ran. An app you opened while the list sat there no longer slips through with files it's holding open, and the Running badge clears as soon as you quit it.
New
Move a license to a new Mac yourself — if activation says the license is already in use, you now get a link to release it from the other Mac. Useful when that Mac was sold, erased or died, which is usually why you're activating a new one.

September 21, 2026

Version 1.6.5
Improved
More thorough cleanup — Notion's workspace cache is now found. It sits under Application Support rather than with your browser data, so no other cleaner looks there and nothing clears it on its own. It's left untouched while Notion is open.

September 15, 2026

Version 1.6.4
Improved
More thorough cleanup — finds cache that other cleaners miss in WeChat, WeCom, Lark and Codex, including crash-report backlogs that can quietly grow to tens of gigabytes. Final Cut Pro proxy media is now listed too, left unticked so you decide whether it's worth re-rendering.
Improved
System Health now tells you what's slowing your Mac down. Instead of repeating a number you can already see, it names the apps holding your memory, spots virtual machines reserving memory while sitting idle, and flags processes that have been stuck running for hours.
Improved
Safer deletions — every removal, including ones that need your password, is re-checked against the protection rules at the moment it runs, and the app now tells you why anything was kept.

September 11, 2026

Version 1.6.3
Improved
More thorough scanning — better protection for browser extensions and for apps you have open while cleaning, plus fuller coverage of Final Cut Pro, Motion and Compressor.

September 8, 2026

Version 1.6.2
Fix
Minor bug fixes and stability improvements

September 6, 2026

Version 1.6.0
Improved
Safer & smarter cleaning — Better protection checks, more accurate results, and fewer unnecessary password prompts.
Improved
Better Mac performance insights — Quickly see your Mac's health and which apps are using the most resources.
Improved
Smarter app removal — Better handling of running apps, security software, Homebrew apps, and leftover files.
Improved
More thorough cleanup — Finds more junk from popular apps, developer tools, and Xcode.
Fix
Improved reliability across Trash, scans, Disk Analyzer, macOS updates, and app leftovers.

July 22, 2026

Version 1.5.2
New
Updated pricing: 1-Year License now $9/year, Lifetime License now $19 one-time
Fix
Minor bug fixes and stability improvements

June 5, 2026

Version 1.5.1
Fix
Bug fixes and stability improvements

May 21, 2026

Version 1.5.0
New
Startup Items Manager - Discover and toggle startup services (Launch Agents, Launch Daemons, and Login Items) directly from the app. Easily identify and disable unwanted startup items to speed up boot time.

May 17, 2026

Version 1.4.6
Improved
Fixed an issue where some apps (e.g., TestFlight apps) couldn't be deleted. The app will now prompt for your admin password when extra permissions are needed to remove protected apps.

May 1, 2026

Version 1.4.3
New
Added "Write a Review" option to the Help menu for easy access to leave feedback on MacUpdate

April 28, 2026

Version 1.4.1
Improved
Enhanced Dashboard: Real-time CPU temperature, battery status with time remaining, and live network upload/download speeds - all in a redesigned layout with combined metric cards for CPU + Temperature, Memory + Total RAM, Battery, and Network.

April 24, 2026

Version 1.4.0
New
Secure Shredder: Permanently destroy sensitive files beyond recovery — AES-256 encryption and multi-pass overwriting ensure deleted files can never be restored. Drag and drop files or browse to select them.
New
Disk Space Analyzer: Visualize what's eating your disk with an interactive squarified treemap. Drill into any folder, spot the biggest space hogs, and delete files directly from the map.
Improved
Onboarding flow updated to introduce all eight modules including the new Shredder and Disk Space Analyzer.
Fix
Sidebar no longer collapses or loses icons when viewing Updater app details.

April 23, 2026

Version 1.3.0
New
App Resetter: Reset any app to its freshly installed state — removes preferences, caches, containers, and support files while keeping the app itself. Files are categorized by risk level so you know exactly what you're deleting.
New
Full Disk Access detection: Cleaner now detects whether FDA is granted and shows an actionable banner to guide you. Protected paths are automatically skipped when not granted, so scans never silently fail.
Improved
Smarter app discovery for Uninstaller and Resetter — recursive scanning finds nested apps like Adobe Creative Cloud helpers, and bundle ID prefix matching catches more leftover data in Caches, Logs, and Application Support.
Improved
Updater sidebar now shows one-click "Update" and "Open" buttons directly in the app list — no need to open the detail view first.
Improved
Cleaner review sheet now shows skipped categories with reasons (e.g. "Xcode is running") so you can see exactly what was excluded and why.
Improved
Redesigned navigation with reordered sidebar and descriptive subtitles for every module, making it easier to find what you need at a glance.
New
Refreshed onboarding that walks through all six modules: Smart Cleanup, App Updater, Complete Uninstaller, Duplicate Finder, and App Resetter.

April 22, 2026

Version 1.2.0
New
Duplicate Files Scanner that detects and removes identical files wasting space on your Mac. Includes Quick Scan presets for common folders and auto-select strategies to keep oldest or newest copies.
Improved
App Updater now detects significantly more updates by scanning subdirectories recursively, looking up Homebrew cask versions for non-brew apps like VS Code, Postman, and AnyDesk, and broadening Sparkle feed detection via embedded frameworks.

April 17, 2026

Version 1.1.0
New
App Updater: Scan installed apps for available updates. Supports App Store, Homebrew, and Sparkle update sources

April 15, 2026

Version 1.0.0
New
Deep cleaning engine that scans 200+ macOS cache, log, and temporary file locations.
New
One-click cleaning to safely remove junk files and reclaim disk space.
New
Complete app uninstaller that removes apps along with hidden support files and leftovers.
New
Mac Health Dashboard to monitor CPU, memory, and disk usage in real time.
New
Fast scanning optimized for both Apple Silicon and Intel Macs.
New
Safe cleaning system that protects personal files and critical macOS data.
DeepCleanMac

A powerful native macOS utility to keep your Mac fast, clean, and organized.
